narrative:
The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 25%, meaning it sees roughly a one-in-four chance of serious repayment problems. That is not a certainty, but it was above the bank’s risk limit for this loan, so the application was denied.

The strongest influences on the decision were, in order, the requested repayment period, your checking-account situation, and the amount requested. Your requested duration of six months was far shorter than the approved-applicant average of about nineteen months, and this worked in your favour by lowering estimated risk. Having no checking-account status also lowered risk and is common among approved applicants, at about 59%. The requested amount of 3,518 DM was somewhat above the approved average of about 3,020 DM, yet it too was a risk-lowering factor in the ranking. In other words, the three most influential factors all helped your case; the denial came from other information combining to outweigh those positives.

To improve a future application, ask the lender for specific feedback, provide stronger evidence of stable income and savings, and consider whether reducing the request or adding documentation would address the weaker parts of your profile. Reapply once those areas are stronger.
